rule: Audit rule 1/2 — missing timeout tuning and incorrect cancellation. `CommandKind::Network` exists to classify network work (`crates/fleet-git/src/model/mutation.rs:11`) but is never consulted when choosing a deadline.
summary: Every git invocation, including `fetch`/`pull`/`push`, is killed after a single hard-coded 60 s deadline; there is no per-kind timeout and no way for a caller to raise it.
failure_scenario: Push a branch with a few hundred MB of new objects, or fetch a large repository, over a slow or throttled uplink. At exactly 60 s the supervisor is cancelled, the `git` child is SIGKILLed, and the user gets `GitError::Timeout` with no way to retry successfully — the same operation from a shell would have finished. Worse for `pull --rebase` (`may_conflict()`, so it is expected to run long): killing it mid-rebase leaves `.git/rebase-merge` in place, so the next `snapshot()` reports `OperationState::Rebase` and every later mutation refuses until the user aborts by hand.
proposed_fix: Make the deadline a function of `GitCommand::kind`: keep 60 s for `Read`/`Mutation` and give `CommandKind::Network` a much longer budget (or none, relying on `GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT`/`GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME` plus caller-side cancellation). Store it as a `Runner` field so tests and callers can override it, and carry the actual value into `GitError::Timeout`.
test_plan: Add to the existing `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod tests` in `crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs` (which already builds a `Runner { git_program: "/bin/sh".into(), ..Runner::default() }`): after the fix expose `read_timeout`/`network_timeout` fields, set `read_timeout = 100ms` and `network_timeout = 5s`, then run `GitCommand::new(temp_dir(), CommandKind::Network).args(["-c", "sleep 0.5"])` and assert it returns `Ok`. Add the mirror case with `CommandKind::Read` asserting `Err(GitError::Timeout { .. })`. The Network case fails today (one shared `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`) and passes after the fix. Also add `assert!(network_timeout > read_timeout)` as a cheap regression guard.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs:27 defines a single `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60)` and it is the only deadline in `Runner::run` (command.rs:301, error at :354); `specification.kind` is never consulted there, and `CommandKind::Network` (crates/fleet-git/src/model/mutation.rs:5-11) is used only for classification/logging. `Runner`'s fields are `inner`, `git_program`, `env`, `output_limit` (command.rs:162-167) and `Runner::new` is private (command.rs:183), so no caller can raise it. fetch/pull/push all go through this runner (crates/fleet-git/src/mutation/network.rs:9,20,34) and are user-reachable from the lazygit UI (crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/mutations.rs:5,19, root/overlays.rs:226, bridge.rs:1057-1058). On timeout the child is SIGKILLed (command.rs:568-570), so a killed `pull --rebase` really can leave `.git/rebase-merge` behind. Nothing in docs/ documents a 60 s git deadline (grep over docs/*.md finds only unrelated 90 s/1 s timeouts), so this is not a documented intentional choice. Note the daemon's own git work uses a separate ShellCommand runner (crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/git.rs), so the blast radius is the lazygit path, not clone/bootstrap.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs (Runner fields, Default/new, the timeout call site and GitError::Timeout construction), crates/fleet-git/src/error.rs:46-51 if the reported value changes, the `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod tests` in command.rs (shell_runner uses struct-update syntax `..Runner::default()`, so new fields must have defaults), and any place constructing a Runner: crates/fleet-git/src/repository.rs (`discover_with_runner`) and crates/fleet-git/tests/*.
corrected_fix: Add `read_timeout` and `network_timeout` fields to `Runner` (defaults 60 s and, say, 10 min), pick per `specification.kind` at command.rs:301, and report the value actually used in `GitError::Timeout`. Keep the fields crate-private with a `pub(crate)`/test-only setter rather than widening the public API — `Runner::new` is deliberately private and the finding's 'expose read_timeout/network_timeout fields' should not become public surface. Do NOT remove the network deadline entirely: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is already set (command.rs:240) but an SSH askpass or a stalled TCP connection would otherwise hang the mutation lock forever, so an unbounded network op needs caller-side cancellation first, which does not exist yet (`CancellationGuard` is internal to `run`). The proposed test using `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 0.5'` works with the existing `shell_runner()` harness but adds ~0.6 s of real sleeping to the suite; prefer `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` only if the child spawn still completes — otherwise keep the sleeps short.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiables / rust-workspace-architecture: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it — the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment saying the receiver is gone only during shutdown."
summary: The reword transaction's rollback (`git rebase --abort`) discards its `Result` entirely, so a failed abort leaves the repository stopped mid-rebase while the caller is told only about the original error.
failure_scenario: `reword_commit` runs `[rebase --interactive, commit --amend, rebase --continue]`. Step 2 fails — e.g. a `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hook exits non-zero, or `--amend` hits an index lock. The repository is at this point stopped at an `edit` stop with `.git/rebase-merge` present and HEAD detached. `rebase --abort` is then attempted and its result thrown away; if it also fails (another process holds `index.lock`, or the worktree has an unmergeable change), the user receives only "commit failed", the daemon logs nothing about the failed rollback, and the worktree is silently left detached mid-rebase. Every later mutation on that repository then fails for a reason the error never names.
proposed_fix: Match on the abort result and either fold it into the returned error or log it: `if let Err(abort) = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await { tracing::warn!(%abort, "failed to abort the rebase started for reword"); }`. Better still, surface it to the caller via `MutationResult::warning`, since "your repo is still mid-rebase" is exactly what the user must be told.
test_plan: Add a test in `crates/fleet-git/tests/` (beside `bugfix_mutation.rs`) using a real temp repo: install a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` that exits 1 so `commit --amend` fails, then call `reword_commit`. Assert the returned error mentions the amend failure AND that the abort outcome is observable — either `MutationResult::warning` is set, or the abort's `CommandRecord` appears in `repository.recent_commands()` with a non-`Success` outcome that the caller can see. Today the abort's outcome is unreachable from the return value, so the assertion on it fails before the fix.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs:117-120 discards the `Result` of `runner.run(rebase_control_command("--abort"))` with a bare `let _ =` and no comment; this is a subprocess call, not the channel-send exception CLAUDE.md carves out, so it is a straight violation of the non-negotiable. Two of the finding's supporting claims are wrong and must not be repeated in a fix: (1) 'the daemon logs nothing about the failed rollback' — `Runner::run` records every non-accepted exit as `CommandOutcome::Failed` and calls `log.finished` (command.rs:391-405) before returning `GitError::Exit`, and that record is broadcast and reachable via `Repository::recent_commands()` (crates/fleet-git/src/repository.rs:102, consumed at crates/fleet-lazygit/src/bridge.rs:547), so the lazygit command-log panel already shows the failed abort; (2) the test plan's fallback assertion ('the abort's CommandRecord appears in recent_commands with a non-Success outcome') therefore already passes today and would not be a regression test. The genuine gap is narrower: the abort failure never reaches the returned `Result`/`MutationResult`, and there is no tracing event, so a caller that only inspects the error cannot tell the worktree was left mid-rebase.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs only for the logging form. If the outcome is surfaced through `MutationResult` instead, it touches crates/fleet-git/src/model/mutation.rs:16-21 semantics ('Successful but notable Git output') and every consumer of `MutationResult::warning` in crates/fleet-lazygit/src/bridge.rs and root/mutations.rs; a new test would go in crates/fleet-git/tests/ next to bugfix_mutation.rs.
corrected_fix: Match the abort result and log it fully qualified: `if let Err(abort) = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await { tracing::warn!(%abort, "failed to abort the rebase started for reword; the worktree is left mid-rebase"); }`. Do not route it through `MutationResult::warning` as the finding suggests: that field is documented as 'successful but notable Git output' and the reword path returns `Err(error)` here, so no `MutationResult` is produced at all on this branch — the warning would have to be smuggled into a success value that does not exist. If the caller must learn the repo is still mid-rebase, extend `GitError` (or wrap the original error's message) rather than repurposing `warning`. A regression test should assert on the returned error / a tracing capture, not on `recent_commands()`, which already contains the failed abort record today.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call. Propagate with `?`, log with a helper, or `match` explicitly" (the fire-and-forget exception requires a comment saying the receiver is gone only during shutdown)
summary: The reword transaction's rollback discards the result of `git rebase --abort`, so a failed abort leaves the repository stuck mid-rebase and the user sees only the original error, with nothing logged about the failed cleanup.
failure_scenario: `git commit --amend` fails mid-transaction (e.g. a pre-commit hook exits non-zero) and the rollback `git rebase --abort` also fails — a stale `.git/index.lock` from a concurrent editor, or an `ORIG_HEAD` that cannot be restored. `abort`'s error is dropped; the caller surfaces only "commit --amend failed", while `.git/rebase-merge/` is still on disk. Every subsequent git operation in that worktree fails with "a rebase is in progress", and there is no log line naming the abort as the thing that failed.
proposed_fix: `if let Err(abort_error) = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await { tracing::warn!(%abort_error, "rebase --abort failed after a reword rollback; the worktree is still mid-rebase"); }` and include that fact in the returned error so the UI can say the repository needs manual recovery.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs`'s test module, drive `run_reword_transaction` with a fake runner scripted to fail the `--amend` command and to fail `rebase --abort` as well; assert (with a capturing `tracing` subscriber) that a warning naming the abort was emitted. Today nothing is emitted and the test fails.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs:110-125 matches the quote exactly: the rollback is `let _ = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await;` with no comment, and it is not a fire-and-forget channel send, so it is the one case CLAUDE.md names explicitly. Every other `let _ =` in the crate is a channel send or a best-effort kill/wait (command_log.rs:88,93; command.rs:569-570; watch.rs:69), which makes this line the outlier rather than a house style. The mid-rebase-stuck consequence is real: run_reword_transaction holds the mutation lock, and nothing else in the transaction records that `.git/rebase-merge/` survived.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs only for the logging change; if the returned error is enriched, it also reaches crates/fleet-git/src/error.rs, crates/fleet-lazygit consumers of GitError, and the reword tests under crates/fleet-git/tests/.
corrected_fix: Do not warn unconditionally — the first element of the three-command transaction IS the interactive rebase (rebase.rs:99-106), so when that command fails, `git rebase --abort` legitimately exits non-zero with 'no rebase in progress' and an unconditional warn would fire on the most common rollback path. Match explicitly and classify: `if let Err(error) = ... { if is_no_rebase_in_progress(&error) { tracing::debug!(...) } else { tracing::warn!(%error, "rebase --abort failed after a reword rollback; the worktree is still mid-rebase") } }`. Enriching the returned error, as the finding suggests, is a separate API change to MutationResult/GitError and should not ride along unless the UI actually renders it.

rule: Audit rule 1 (real bug: wrong behaviour for a concrete input) — git porcelain parsing that breaks on unusual output; the field that would give the right answer (`%(symref)`) is requested and arity-checked but never read.
summary: `remote_branches` filters the remote's symbolic HEAD by testing `name.ends_with("/HEAD")`, but `%(refname:short)` never produces that suffix for `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, so a remote whose name contains a slash lists its symbolic HEAD as a phantom branch.
failure_scenario: A repository with `git remote add up/stream <url>` (git permits slashes in remote names) and `git remote set-head up/stream main`. `git for-each-ref refs/remotes` emits the symbolic HEAD with `%(refname:short) == "up/stream"`. `ends_with("/HEAD")` is false, `split_once('/')` yields `("up", "stream")`, so the symbolic HEAD is pushed into `groups["up"]` as `RemoteBranch { name: "up/stream", branch: "stream", oid: <main's oid> }`. The lazygit remote-branch pane then shows a phantom branch `stream` under a phantom remote `up`, alongside the real `stream/main`, and checking it out or diffing it targets a symbolic ref. For an ordinary single-segment remote the symref happens to be dropped only by the accidental fallback that `"origin"` contains no `/` — not by the intended guard, which is dead code.
proposed_fix: Replace the name-suffix test with the field the format already requests: `if !fields[4].is_empty() { continue; }` (a non-empty `%(symref)` is exactly "this ref is symbolic"). Fix the colocated test to feed the name git actually emits (`origin` with a non-empty symref field, and `up/stream` for the slashed-remote case) instead of the fabricated `origin/HEAD`.
test_plan:
In `crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs` tests, replace/extend `groups_remote_branches_and_skips_symbolic_head` with input matching real git output:
`b"up/stream/main\x00aaa\x00subject\x001\x00\x00\nup/stream\x00aaa\x00\x000\x00refs/remotes/up/stream/main\x00\n"`
and assert `remote_branches(input)` returns exactly one group whose branches are `["stream/main"]` — i.e. `assert!(groups.iter().all(|g| g.branches.iter().all(|b| b.branch != "stream")))`. This fails today (the symref row is accepted as branch `stream`) and passes after switching the guard to `fields[4]`. Add a second case with `origin`/`refs/remotes/origin/main` asserting the same, which today passes only by accident.
verify_reason: Reproduced against real git 2.55 in a scratch repo: `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)|%(refname:short)|%(symref)' refs/remotes` emits `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD|origin|refs/remotes/origin/main` and `refs/remotes/up/stream/HEAD|up/stream|refs/remotes/up/stream/main` — `%(refname:short)` never ends in `/HEAD`, so the guard at crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs:41 is dead code. `records(input, 5, ...)` (refs.rs:39) arity-checks the `%(symref)` field requested at crates/fleet-git/src/read/refs.rs:36 and nothing ever reads `fields[4]`. The colocated test crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs:192-204 feeds a fabricated `origin/HEAD` record git never produces, so it proves nothing. For an ordinary remote the symref row is dropped only by the accidental `split_once('/')` -> None fallback (refs.rs:43). `git remote add up/stream <url>` is accepted by git (verified), so the phantom-branch input is real. Two corrections to the finding: severity is lower than 'medium' in practice — slash-containing remote names are rare and no ordinary repo is affected; and the phantom row is not the only breakage for such a remote — the real branch `up/stream/main` is also misgrouped as remote `up` / branch `stream/main` by the same `split_once`, which the proposed fix does not address.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs (guard + the `groups_remote_branches_and_skips_symbolic_head` test, whose fixture must be replaced with real git output); if the grouping is fixed too, crates/fleet-git/src/read/refs.rs:29-40 must thread the known remote names into the parser, which changes the concurrent read composition in crates/fleet-git/src/read.rs:66-112 and touches crates/fleet-git/tests/repository.rs:247 and the lazygit consumers crates/fleet-lazygit/src/state/selections.rs:187-195 and panels/side.rs:155-210 (display only, no signature change).
corrected_fix: Replace the suffix test with `if !fields[4].is_empty() { continue; }` (a non-empty `%(symref)` is exactly 'this ref is symbolic'), and rewrite the test fixture to real git output (`origin` and `up/stream` rows carrying a symref, plus the ordinary `origin/main` rows). Do not stop there if slashed remotes are meant to be supported: `split_once('/')` still misattributes `up/stream/main` to remote `up`. Either (a) document that fleet-git assumes single-segment remote names and keep `split_once`, or (b) pass the remote names read by `read_remotes` into `remote_branches` and split on the longest matching remote prefix. Option (a) is the honest minimal change; option (b) is the correct one and costs a signature change.
